Do not scaffold code yet.

actors.name: Owner
actors.description: Adult child who funds the account and authors the constitution (caps, thresholds, allowlists).
actors.interactions: Creates/revokes mandate, edits constitution versions, signs EIP-712 approvals for new payees and above-threshold amounts, freezes payees, reviews evidence.

actors.name: Payer
actors.description: The parent receiving the service; no crypto knowledge, never signs.
actors.interactions: Read-only: sees which bills are handled and settled; may forward an invoice.

actors.name: Agent
actors.description: LLM-driven software that proposes payments from invoices.
actors.interactions: Proposes payment attempts, never holds keys, never edits policy, never chooses command params — code generates them.

actors.name: Payee
actors.description: Utility, insurer, pharmacy, home service, dentist receiving funds.
actors.interactions: Issues invoices with a bank digest; bank-detail changes trigger quarantine.

actors.name: Adversary
actors.interactions: Mutates bank details, splits payments to evade caps, replays invoices, steals an operator key.

actors.name: Operator
actors.description: Whoever holds the Rigorix operator key that dispatches preconditions.
actors.interactions: Runs the governance server; cannot exceed the constitution because the contract is the commit-point lock.

assumptions.assumption: One household, one owner, one payer, one mandate at a time — no multi-tenancy.
assumptions.impactIfWrong: Identity and policy scoping logic explodes; mandate/quarantine lookups lose their simple key.
assumptions.mitigation: Model household_id as a field everywhere but hardcode a single seeded household for the MVP.

assumptions.assumption: Invoices arrive as structured records (seeded fixtures or manual/agent extraction), not a full OCR ingestion pipeline.
assumptions.impactIfWrong: Ingestion becomes the biggest build item and squeezes enforcement work.
assumptions.mitigation: Treat ingestion as a generic/supporting adapter with a seeded fixture set covering all 7 scenarios.

assumptions.assumption: Rigorix OSS rigorix-server is used unmodified; only preconditions.toml, sequence-policy.toml, capacity.toml and signed envelopes are authored by us.
assumptions.impactIfWrong: Forking the server costs hours and breaks the 'no LLM in enforcement' claim.
assumptions.mitigation: Pin the OSS version in hour 0; spike execute/approve/audit.read against it before writing domain code.

assumptions.assumption: The chain adapter can run against local Anvil with a Foundry deploy, so the demo does not depend on live Base Sepolia availability.
assumptions.impactIfWrong: If Anvil parity with Sepolia diverges (USDC address, gas, confirmations), the demo passes locally and fails on the live claim.
assumptions.mitigation: Deploy PaymentRouter to both networks in hour 0; pin chain id, USDC address and confirmation count per network behind ChainNetwork.

boundedContexts.name: Mandate
boundedContexts.description: Owns the household, its parties (owner, payer, agent), the payee registry with verified bank digests, and the immutable constitution versions that define caps, thresholds and approval rules. It is the single source of truth for what is allowed; it never decides a specific payment. Per-context pass COMPLETE: 12 entities (5 aggregate roots, 4 entities, 5 value objects), 8 invariants, 12 domain events, 16 ubiquitous-language terms.
boundedContexts.subdomainRationale: The differentiator is delegated-but-bounded authority; the rules of who may be paid and how much are the product.

invariants.rule: Exactly one constitution version is in force per household at any time.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Two contradictory rule sets both claiming to authorize a payment.

invariants.rule: A published constitution version is immutable; changes create a new version.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Retroactively loosening rules to make an already-refused payment look allowed.

invariants.rule: Only the owner may publish a version, register a payee, re-approve a digest or freeze a payee; the agent holds no such capability.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Agent or stolen operator key editing policy to widen its own authority.

invariants.rule: A payee's verified bank digest only changes through an owner re-approval event.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: A scam invoice silently rebinding a payee to an attacker address.

invariants.rule: Quarantined and frozen payees are never eligible; quarantine cannot be cleared without an owner signature.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: A payment dispatched to a payee whose routing details are disputed.

invariants.rule: Freeze is strictly stronger than quarantine and cannot be downgraded to quarantine.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: A freeze being softened by an automatic transition back to payable.

invariants.rule: A payee registered without an owner-verified address and digest is status new, never eligible.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: First payment to an unverified address passing as a normal auto-pay.

invariants.rule: The payer never holds a signing capability and the agent never holds a key.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Custody drifting to a party who cannot be held accountable for a payment.

boundedContexts.name: Billing
boundedContexts.description: The demand side of the domain: invoices as documents, and payment attempts as the agent's only legal output. Billing owns what is owed and what the agent proposed; it never decides whether a payment is allowed. Its job is to make proposals untrusted, structured and non-duplicable.
boundedContexts.subdomainRationale: Necessary input to the story, but it is bookkeeping over documents; no unique enforcement logic.

invariants.rule: An invoice has at most one non-terminal payment attempt at a time.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Two concurrent attempts racing the same invoice into a double payment.

invariants.rule: An invoice whose attempt settled is closed and cannot spawn further attempts.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Re-paying a bill after a confirmed settlement (scenario 6).

invariants.rule: Payee routing fields on an attempt are copied from Mandate, never from invoice text or agent output.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Invoice-supplied bank details reaching settlement.

invariants.rule: A proposal that supplies a command path, payee address, cap or threshold is rejected outright, not sanitized.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: A prompt injection smuggling parameters into the run_command call.

invariants.rule: Amount must be positive, in USDC, and equal to the invoice amount it references.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Splitting one bill into several attempts with edited amounts to dodge the threshold.

invariants.rule: An invoice hash identifies the bill; a second invoice with the same hash is the same invoice.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Duplicate invoices created by replay entering the funnel as new demand.

invariants.rule: Only an allow or escalate determination can move an attempt to dispatched; a refusal leaves the attempt terminal with no side effect.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: A refused attempt being retried implicitly into a payment.

boundedContexts.name: Authority
boundedContexts.description: The decision engine and the system's heart. Turns an untrusted attempt into a PaymentIntent with code-generated parameters, re-reads the in-force constitution and live payee state at the moment of consequence, issues an allow/deny/escalate Determination with reasons, and holds atomic Reservations against the daily cap until settlement resolves.
boundedContexts.subdomainRationale: Contains the check-at-dispatch-time, atomic-reservation and exact-intent-binding invariants that make the agent safe.

invariants.rule: No dispatch without a Determination whose verdict is allow, taken against the currently in-force constitution version.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Paying on a plan-time decision that the world has since invalidated.

invariants.rule: Committed plus reserved never exceeds the daily cap; the check and the reservation are one atomic step.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Concurrent split attempts each seeing headroom and jointly overdrawing the cap.

invariants.rule: Every payment intent is built from Mandate-owned data; agent-supplied amount, address, digest or command path is discarded, not merged.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Prompt injection substituting the payee address at dispatch.

invariants.rule: A reservation is committed only on confirmed settlement, released only on confirmed non-settlement, and never both.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: A ledger that double-counts or loses money relative to the chain.

invariants.rule: An approval is bound to exactly one intent id plus amount, payee address and bank digest; any mismatch invalidates it.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: An approval for a 20 USDC dentist bill being replayed for a 320 USDC payment elsewhere.

invariants.rule: An approval is single-use and expires; consuming it twice is impossible.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: One owner signature dispatching two payments.

invariants.rule: A refused determination produces no reservation commit, no settlement order and no on-chain transaction, yet is still recorded.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: A refusal that leaves a partial side effect (reserved capacity, queued order).

invariants.rule: Escalation is mandatory when the payee is new or the amount exceeds the threshold; the agent cannot waive it.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Auto-paying a first-time payee because the amount happened to be small.

boundedContexts.name: Settlement
boundedContexts.description: Moves USDC and proves it happened exactly once. Owns the chain adapter, the PaymentRouter call, the nullifier, and the receipt that reconciles the off-chain ledger with the chain. It is the second lock: even a stolen operator key cannot make it pay a payee the contract rejects, exceed an on-chain allowance, or pay the same invoice twice.
boundedContexts.subdomainRationale: The on-chain second lock and exactly-once settlement is the second half of the safety claim.

invariants.rule: A SettlementOrder can only be created from a determination with verdict allow (or escalate that became ApprovalGranted) for the same intent id.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Dispatching a payment that was never authorized.

invariants.rule: The run_command path is a code constant; its parameters are generated from the PaymentIntent, never accepted from the agent or a config the agent can write.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: An injection redirecting the settlement command or its arguments.

invariants.rule: An invoice settles at most once: the nullifier is derived from the invoice hash, duplicated locally and enforced by the contract at the commit point.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: A replayed duplicate invoice draining funds (scenario 6).

invariants.rule: One order maps to exactly one transaction; a submission is never retried with a new nonce for the same intent.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: A retry loop paying twice after a timeout looks like a failure.

invariants.rule: A receipt is only final after the configured confirmation count; a pending receipt never commits cap.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Counting a reorged-away payment as settled.

invariants.rule: Contract revert on a nullifier is a refusal, not an error to retry.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Error-handling paths that resurrect a duplicate payment.

invariants.rule: The payee address used for settlement is the one stored in the PaymentIntent, never re-read from the invoice at submit time.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Late substitution of the destination between authorization and signature.

boundedContexts.name: Evidence
boundedContexts.description: Capture-and-verify context: appends a signed HMAC envelope for every attempt, determination, refusal, approval, settlement and revert, and anchors envelope hashes on-chain. It consumes events from Authority, Settlement and Billing and publishes verification for the console and auditors. It holds no enforcement power — it is a witness, not a guard.
boundedContexts.subdomainRationale: Crucial for trust and demo, but it is capture-and-verify plumbing over the other contexts' events.

invariants.rule: Every payment attempt produces at least one envelope, including attempts that were refused before any determination.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: A silent refusal with no record, making the system unauditable (principle 5).

invariants.rule: Envelopes are append-only; corrections are new envelopes referencing the previous hash.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Rewriting history to hide a misdispatch.

invariants.rule: An envelope's hash must match its on-chain anchor, and a single altered byte must fail verification.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Locally consistent but externally forged audit trail (scenario 7).

invariants.rule: A refusal is recorded with the same rigor as a settlement: same envelope shape, same anchor treatment.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Refusals becoming second-class and dropping out of the proof.

invariants.rule: The HMAC key is operator-held and never present in the agent workspace or any envelope payload.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: The agent forging its own evidence.

boundedContexts.name: Console
boundedContexts.description: API/UI composition and read models for owner and payer. No business rules; projects other contexts' state.
boundedContexts.subdomainRationale: Pure presentation/composition; rules live elsewhere by principle 7.

contextMap.note: Authority reads the in-force constitution version and live payee eligibility at dispatch time; re-read, never cached, per 'authority re-read at moment of consequence'.
Attempts arrive as untrusted agent proposals; Authority translates them into PaymentIntents and discards agent-supplied amounts, addresses and command params.
Settlement may only execute an order derived from an allow determination; both sides co-evolve around the intent_id contract and the commit-or-release outcome.
Settlement uses the payee address carried on the PaymentIntent, which originates from Mandate's verified bank digest — never from invoice text.
Settlement publishes receipts and reverts for enveloping and asks Evidence to anchor the hash; anchoring is the shared on-chain write both contexts name 'anchor'.
Invoices reference a Mandate-issued payee id and present a bank digest for comparison; invoice text is never authoritative for routing.
Authority publishes determinations and refusals; Evidence consumes and seals them.
Console consumes read models and submits approvals; it cannot trigger a payment directly.
Evidence exposes verification endpoints the console renders for the owner and payer.
Console reads constitution and payee status for display only; it may request a version but the owner signature is what publishes it.

openQuestions: Resolved by modeling: quarantine is payee-level but the baseline digest only changes via owner re-approval (PayeeReapproved); an approval is single-use and expiring, so a transient refusal requires a fresh signature; the nullifier is derived from the invoice hash and enforced by the contract, with Settlement reconciling from receipts. Still open: (1) does a revert release the reservation immediately or after a reconciliation sweep? (2) is the simulated bank payout a Settlement concern or a Console label only? (3) does Evidence own the HMAC key or receive it from operator config at boot? (4) how many confirmations does the demo claim on Sepolia before calling a receipt final?

functionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall let the owner create exactly one mandate naming the owner address, payer, agent identity and the in-force constitution version.
The system shall keep constitution versions immutable and append-only, and shall allow only the owner to publish a new version.
The system shall reject any attempt to modify the constitution that originates from the agent or the console.
The system shall record payees with an owner-verified address and a bank digest computed over payee routing details.
The system shall quarantine a payee when an invoice presents a bank digest that differs from the verified digest, and shall block payments to it until the owner re-approves.
The system shall allow the owner to freeze a payee, and a frozen payee shall be ineligible at dispatch even if it was eligible at plan time.
The system shall record invoices with payee reference, amount, currency, due date, invoice hash and the bank digest as presented.
The system shall refuse a second payment attempt for an invoice already settled or in flight, and the contract shall independently revert a duplicate nullifier.
The system shall accept agent proposals only as structured payment attempts and shall never accept agent-supplied command paths, payee addresses or caps.
The system shall generate the run_command invocation and its parameters in code from the payment intent, never from LLM output.
The system shall produce an authority determination (allow, deny or escalate) for every payment attempt before dispatch, and shall block dispatch when no allow determination exists.
The system shall re-read the in-force constitution version and live payee status at dispatch time rather than trusting a plan-time decision.
The system shall reserve funds atomically so that committed plus reserved never exceeds the daily cap, and shall refuse any attempt that would breach it.
The system shall escalate a payment to owner signature when the payee is new or the amount exceeds the threshold.
The system shall bind an approval to one exact intent id, amount, payee address and bank digest, and shall invalidate the approval if any of those change.
The system shall verify owner approval signatures as EIP-712 typed data off-chain before dispatch, and the contract shall verify the same signature on-chain.
The system shall commit or release a reservation according to the settlement outcome so the cap ledger stays consistent with the chain.
The system shall guarantee a refusal produces no on-chain transaction and no reservation commit, while still being recorded.
The system shall dispatch exactly one PaymentRouter transaction per allow determination using USDC on Base Sepolia, with a local Anvil fallback.
The system shall record a chain receipt (tx hash, block, confirmations, status) for every dispatched order and expose it for verification.
The system shall prevent an invoice from settling more than once on-chain by nullifier enforcement in the contract and nullifier reconciliation in the service.
The system shall emit a signed HMAC evidence envelope for every attempt, determination, refusal, approval and settlement.
The system shall anchor each envelope hash on-chain and shall fail verification when any byte of the envelope is altered.
The system shall render for the owner an approval inbox showing the exact intent fields to be signed.
The system shall render for the payer a read-only view of handled and settled bills with plain-language status and a simulated bank payout label.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall decide and dispatch a payment attempt within a bounded latency suitable for a live demo.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: Determination returned in under 500 ms p95; end-to-end confirm on Base Sepolia under 30 s, Anvil under 3 s.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: No LLM shall appear in the enforcement path.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: Zero LLM calls between attempt submission and on-chain dispatch, enforced by a test asserting no model dependency in Authority or Settlement.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall keep the agent unable to write to the authority service or the policy files.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: Precondition client lives outside the agent-writable workspace; agent has no write access to .rigorix/ or the SQLite DB.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall produce tamper-evident evidence with independent on-chain time.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: 100% of decisions enveloped; one flipped byte fails verification; anchor transaction recorded per envelope hash.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall be resilient to duplicate and replayed submissions.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: Zero successful second settlements across a replay suite of at least 10 replays.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall expose an API-first boundary so the frontend can be built against mocks in parallel.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: OpenAPI schema published by hour 6; frontend runs against mocks with no backend changes required at integration.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The domain model shall fit the 24-hour timebox including demo rehearsal.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: Code freeze met with all 7 acceptance scenarios green and no stretch capability blocking the demo path.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall run locally with no external paid dependency.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: Full scenario suite runnable on Anvil plus SQLite on a laptop; Base Sepolia used for the live claim only.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall keep cap accounting exactly consistent with the chain.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: Committed plus reserved ledger equals on-chain settled total within one confirmation of every transaction, verified by a reconciliation test.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall keep the enforcement path auditable by any third party from the repo alone.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: Every precondition, constitution rule and EIP-712 struct readable in the repo with no hidden fallback path; verifier reproducible from a clean clone.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall keep the owner's approval flow usable on a phone in under a minute.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: Owner signs an escalated payment in at most 3 taps after opening the notification; measured in the demo run.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall degrade predictably when the chain is unavailable.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: RPC failure yields a refusal-or-pending determination with no reservation commit; no attempt is silently dropped.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall keep evidence write cost bounded during the demo.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: Anchoring limited to the demo scenario envelopes; remaining envelopes batched and labeled as batched.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall keep the authority service simple enough for a 24-hour build.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: Single process, SQLite, no message broker, no background job framework; refusal paths unit-testable without a chain.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall never lose an attempt: every submitted attempt has a terminal state.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: Zero attempts in a non-terminal state older than 10 minutes in the demo database after the full scenario run.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall keep the agent's blast radius to proposals only.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: Agent credentials cannot write payee status, constitution, reservations or evidence; verified by an authorization test matrix.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall keep payer-facing copy free of crypto jargon.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: Zero terms from the crypto vocabulary list on payer screens; reviewed against the UL glossary before freeze.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall be demonstrable from a clean checkout.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: docker-compose or make targets bring up Anvil, authority service and console in under 5 minutes on the demo machine.

applicationServices.name: CreateMandate
applicationServices.useCase: Owner establishes the household mandate: registers owner address, payer, agent identity and the first constitution version.

applicationServices.name: PublishConstitutionVersion
applicationServices.useCase: Owner appends a new immutable constitution version with caps, thresholds and approval rules; the previous version is superseded but retained.

applicationServices.name: RegisterPayee
applicationServices.useCase: Owner registers a payee with a verified payout address and bank digest, establishing the trusted routing baseline.

applicationServices.name: QuarantinePayee
applicationServices.useCase: Reacts to a bank-digest mismatch by suspending the payee until the owner re-approves the new routing details.
commands: compare presented digest to verified digest

applicationServices.name: FreezePayee
applicationServices.useCase: Owner freezes a payee so it becomes ineligible at the next dispatch even if it was eligible when the payment was planned.

applicationServices.name: RecordInvoice
applicationServices.useCase: Registers an invoice with amount, due date, invoice hash and the bank digest as presented, without trusting it for routing.

applicationServices.name: ProposePayment
applicationServices.useCase: Translates an agent proposal into a structured payment attempt, rejecting any agent-supplied routing or policy field.
commands: check invoice not already settled or in flight

applicationServices.name: EvaluateAuthority
applicationServices.useCase: The core decision: builds a payment intent from the attempt, re-reads the in-force constitution and live payee state, and issues allow, deny or escalate with reasons.
commands: check payee allowlist and digest match
check amount against threshold and caps

applicationServices.name: ReserveCapacity
applicationServices.useCase: Atomically reserves amount against the daily cap so committed plus reserved never exceeds it; refuses rather than over-books.

applicationServices.name: EscalateForSignature
applicationServices.useCase: Converts an escalate determination into a signature request bound to the exact intent id, amount, address and bank digest.

applicationServices.name: SubmitOwnerSignature
applicationServices.useCase: Verifies the owner's EIP-712 signature against the exact bound intent and either authorises dispatch or refuses without side effect.

applicationServices.name: ReconcileReservation
applicationServices.useCase: Commits or releases a reservation according to the settlement outcome so the cap ledger matches the chain.

applicationServices.name: DispatchPayment
applicationServices.useCase: Executes the allow-determined order through Rigorix run_command with a code-generated command path, then submits the PaymentRouter transaction.

applicationServices.name: SettleOnce
applicationServices.useCase: Enforces exactly-once settlement by deriving the invoice nullifier, rejecting local duplicates and relying on the contract revert as the final lock.

applicationServices.name: SealEvidence
applicationServices.useCase: Wraps every attempt, determination, refusal, approval and settlement into a signed HMAC envelope and anchors its hash on-chain.

applicationServices.name: VerifyEvidence
applicationServices.useCase: Re-verifies an envelope for an auditor or the console and detects any single-byte tampering or anchor mismatch.

applicationServices.name: ProjectApprovalInbox
applicationServices.useCase: Read-model projection for the owner of pending signature requests with exact intent details; carries no business rules.

applicationServices.name: ReapprovePayeeDigest
applicationServices.useCase: Owner signs off on the new bank details; the verified digest baseline is replaced and the payee returns to eligible.
commands: verify owner signature on new digest

applicationServices.name: ProjectPayerBills
applicationServices.useCase: Read-only projection for the payer of handled and settled bills in household language, with the simulated bank payout labeled.

domainEvents.name: MandateCreated
domainEvents.description: A household mandate exists with owner, payer, agent and first constitution version.

domainEvents.name: ConstitutionVersionPublished
domainEvents.description: A new immutable rule set is in force; the previous version is superseded.

domainEvents.name: PayeeRegistered
domainEvents.description: A payee with a verified address and bank digest entered the allowlist as new.

domainEvents.name: PayeeDigestChanged
domainEvents.description: An invoice presented routing details that differ from the verified bank digest.

domainEvents.name: PayeeQuarantined
domainEvents.description: Payee is ineligible until the owner re-approves the new routing details; any in-flight intent for it must fail at dispatch.

domainEvents.name: PayeeFrozen
domainEvents.description: Owner suspended a payee; it cannot be paid at all until unfrozen.

domainEvents.name: PayeeReapproved
domainEvents.description: Owner signed off on the new bank details; the digest baseline is replaced and the payee returns to eligible.

domainEvents.name: InvoiceRecorded
domainEvents.description: A bill entered the system with its hash, amount and presented bank digest.

domainEvents.name: DuplicateInvoiceDetected
domainEvents.description: An invoice hash already known arrived again; the second one is not treated as new demand.

domainEvents.name: PaymentProposed
domainEvents.description: The agent produced a structured attempt for an invoice; this is the request that Authority must judge.

domainEvents.name: ProposalRejected
domainEvents.description: The proposal was malformed or carried forbidden fields and was rejected before any determination was requested.

domainEvents.name: AttemptDispatched
domainEvents.description: An attempt moved to dispatched after an allow determination; recorded locally for lifecycle only, settlement truth lives in Settlement.

domainEvents.name: InvoiceSettled
domainEvents.description: The invoice is closed as paid and can no longer generate attempts.

domainEvents.name: AttemptRefused
domainEvents.description: The attempt ended refused; the invoice returns to outstanding for a future legitimate proposal.

domainEvents.name: PaymentIntentIssued
domainEvents.description: A code-constructed intent exists with the exact fields that will be signed and enforced.

domainEvents.name: AuthorityDetermined
domainEvents.description: The verdict for an intent, with reason codes and the constitution version consulted at dispatch time.

domainEvents.name: PaymentAllowed
domainEvents.description: The only event that can authorize dispatch; Settlement refuses to move without it.

domainEvents.name: PaymentRefused
domainEvents.description: A refusal with its reason: digest mismatch, payee quarantined or frozen, cap exceeded, duplicate invoice, invalid approval, no owner signature.

domainEvents.name: CapacityReserved
domainEvents.description: Amount held against the daily cap for a specific intent.

domainEvents.name: CapacityRefused
domainEvents.description: The cap headroom check failed; the attempt is refused without reserving anything.

domainEvents.name: ApprovalRequested
domainEvents.description: An escalation opened a signature request bound to one exact intent.

domainEvents.name: ApprovalGranted
domainEvents.description: The owner's EIP-712 signature verified against the bound intent; the intent may now be dispatched.

domainEvents.name: ApprovalRejected
domainEvents.description: Signature invalid, signer not the owner, or the binding did not match; the attempt is refused with no side effect.

domainEvents.name: ApprovalExpired
domainEvents.description: The signature window closed before dispatch; the owner must re-sign a fresh intent.

domainEvents.name: CapacityCommitted
domainEvents.description: A reservation became committed spend after settled settlement.

domainEvents.name: CapacityReleased
domainEvents.description: A reservation was released because settlement did not happen; the cap headroom returns.

domainEvents.name: SettlementOrdered
domainEvents.description: An allowed intent became an executable order with its nullifier and code-generated command.

domainEvents.name: SettlementSubmitted
domainEvents.description: The transaction was broadcast; a tx hash now exists and the outstanding window begins.

domainEvents.name: SettlementConfirmed
domainEvents.description: The receipt reached the required confirmations; this is the only event that can commit cap and close an invoice.

domainEvents.name: SettlementReverted
domainEvents.description: The contract rejected the transaction, typically a duplicate nullifier or a failed on-chain precondition; treated as a refusal.

domainEvents.name: DuplicateSettlementBlocked
domainEvents.description: The nullifier was already spent, locally or on-chain; nothing moved.

domainEvents.name: NullifierSpent
domainEvents.description: The invoice's once-only marker is now consumed for this mandate scope.

domainEvents.name: ReceiptAnchored
domainEvents.description: A settlement receipt or evidence hash was written on-chain, giving independent integrity and time.

domainEvents.name: EnvelopeSealed
domainEvents.description: A domain fact was wrapped, signed and appended to the audit trail.

domainEvents.name: EnvelopeAnchored
domainEvents.description: The envelope hash was written on-chain, fixing its integrity and time independently of the operator.

domainEvents.name: EvidenceVerificationFailed
domainEvents.description: A re-verification did not match the sealed envelope or its anchor, indicating tampering or corruption.

domainEvents.name: OwnerRegistered
domainEvents.description: The owner address is bound to the household and becomes the sole signature authority.

domainEvents.name: PayerEnrolled
domainEvents.description: The parent is enrolled as the beneficiary of the service; no signing capability is granted.

domainEvents.name: AgentAuthorised
domainEvents.description: A software identity is granted proposal-only authority, bounded by the current constitution version.

domainEvents.name: CapChanged
domainEvents.description: A new constitution version sets a different daily ceiling; in-flight reservations continue under the version they were reserved against.

domainEvents.name: ThresholdChanged
domainEvents.description: A new constitution version changes the auto-pay limit, shifting which future payments must be escalated.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: The adult child who funds the account and authors the constitution. The only party who can change rules, add payees or approve exceptions.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Owner signs an EIP-712 approval for a new dentist payee.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: The parent whose bills are being paid. Receives the service, holds no keys, signs nothing.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Payer sees a read-only list of settled bills.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Software identity that may only propose payments. Holds no keys and cannot edit policy or command paths.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Agent proposes five attempts for the same utility invoice.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: The scoped, revocable grant of authority from owner to agent, pinned to one constitution version lineage and one household.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: The mandate permits paying enrolled payees up to 50 USDC/day.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: The operator-owned rule set the enforcement layer checks: caps, thresholds, allowlist, signature requirements. Immutable per version, append-only lineage.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Constitution v3 raises the per-payment threshold to 100 USDC.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: A registered biller with a verified payout address, a verified bank digest and an eligibility status.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: The pharmacy is a payee in status eligible.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Hash over payee routing details. Replaces raw account numbers in every downstream check; a mismatch is the bank-detail-change scam signal.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Invoice presents digest 9f2c… but the payee's verified digest is 41ab…

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Payee-level suspension triggered automatically by a bank-digest mismatch; cleared only by an owner re-approval.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: The scam invoice quarantines the utility instead of redirecting the money.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Owner-initiated payee suspension. Strictly stronger than quarantine and never automatic.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Owner freezes the insurer after a dispute.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: The maximum total USDC that may be committed plus reserved within a rolling day, summed across all payees.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Cap of 150 USDC/day refuses the sixth 40 USDC split invoice.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: The per-payment amount above which an owner signature is mandatory, regardless of payee status.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Threshold 25 USDC; a 320 USDC bill escalates to the owner.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: A bill document presented for payment, identified by its content hash, carrying amount, due date and a presented bank digest that is never authoritative for routing.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: The utility invoice for 42.50 USDC due Friday.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Canonical content hash of an invoice. Serves as the duplicate key off-chain and the nullifier seed on-chain.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Hash 0x8c1f… appears twice → duplicate detected before the funnel.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: The agent's structured proposal to pay one invoice. Exists only to be judged; it carries no authority and cannot dispatch itself.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Attempt 7 for invoice 12, 42.50 USDC, payee utility.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: When the agent submits, the only accepted shape is a payment attempt; anything else is a proposal rejection, not a negotiation.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: A proposal containing a command path is rejected, not sanitized.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: The invoice already has an attempt that has been dispatched or is awaiting signature; a second attempt is refused locally.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Six split invoices run concurrently; only the first that reserves wins.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: The digest of routing details as they appear on the invoice. Compared against Mandate's verified digest; mismatch means quarantine.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: The poisoned invoice presents an attacker digest.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: One real obligation broken into several invoices each below the threshold. Detected by the aggregate daily cap, not by per-invoice heuristics.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Six invoices of 25 USDC against a 150 USDC cap.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: The code-constructed, immutable description of one payment: intent id, invoice id, payee, payee address, amount, bank digest, is_new_payee, requires_owner_signature. The unit of authority and of signature binding.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Intent 0xab… for 320 USDC to the insurer, requires_owner_signature true.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: The allow/deny/escalate verdict for one intent, produced at dispatch time against the in-force constitution and live payee state, with reason codes.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: deny / digital_digest_mismatch / constitution v3 / payee quarantined.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: An atomic hold of amount against the daily cap for one intent; committed or released exactly once after settlement resolves.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Six 25 USDC attempts against a 150 USDC cap: the sixth is refused.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: An owner EIP-712 signature over an intent's exact fields; single-use, expiring, and invalid the moment the intent changes.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Owner signs the new payee and 320 USDC amount in one typed-data payload.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: The verdict for a payment that is not refused but cannot proceed without the owner: new payee or above threshold.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: escalate / new_payee / requires_owner_signature true.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: The instant a precondition check is bound to the dispatch. Authority must re-read all external state here, not at plan time.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Payee frozen between approval and dispatch → refused at this moment.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Spend that has been confirmed on-chain and permanently counts against the day's cap.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Two settled invoices, 85 USDC committed.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Returning reserved capacity to the ledger because the payment provably did not happen. Never a rollback of committed spend.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Chain revert releases the 42.50 USDC reservation.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Flag on the intent, derived from Mandate's payee status, that forces escalation regardless of amount.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: First payment to the dentist is new → escalate.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Flag on the intent that the contract also checks on-chain; the off-chain determination and the contract must agree.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Set true for new payees and above-threshold amounts.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: The confirmed on-chain movement of USDC from the household account to a payee address under one nullifier.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: 42.50 USDC settled in tx 0x3d… on Base Sepolia.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: The immutable executable form of an allowed intent, carrying payee address, amount, nullifier and the code-generated command reference.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Order 12 derived from intent 0xab…

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Derived once-only marker from the invoice hash; the on-chain anti-double-pay key. Spending it twice is impossible by construction.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Replaying invoice 12 hits a spent nullifier and reverts.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: The chain proof for an order: tx hash, block, confirmations, status, and the anchor written for its evidence envelope.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Receipt confirms 6 blocks and anchor tx 0x9e…

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: The property that PaymentRouter, not the app, is the final gate: whatever the off-chain state, a bad payment cannot be mined.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: A stolen operator key still cannot pay a frozen payee address.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Blocks mined after the transaction's inclusion; only after the required count is the settlement final and the cap committed.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Anvil needs 1, Base Sepolia needs 2 for the demo.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: The Rigorix payment step: a fixed command path plus structured params generated by code from the intent.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: run_command('payments.dispatch', intent_id, payee_address, amount_usdc, bank_digest, …)

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: On-chain rejection of a settlement, most often a duplicate nullifier or a failed signature check. Always a refusal with evidence, never a retry.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Contract reverts with NullifierSpent.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: The on-chain write of an envelope hash that gives tamper evidence an independent timestamp.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Envelope hash 0x77… anchored in tx 0x9e…

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Signed immutable wrapper around one domain fact, containing subject ids, the fact payload, the constitution version consulted and an HMAC.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Envelope for a refusal: deny / payee_frozen / constitution v3.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: Canonical hash of an envelope including its HMAC; what gets anchored on-chain and re-compared at verification.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Flip one byte of the payload → hash no longer matches the anchor.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: The on-chain record of an envelope hash, giving independent integrity and time that the operator cannot rewrite.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Anchor tx 0x9e… contains hash 0x77…

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: A first-class evidence artifact for a denied payment, carrying the reason code and the constitution version that produced it.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: The poisoned-invoice refusal is demoed as a verified envelope, not an absence.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: HMAC proves no one in the operator domain edited the record; the anchor proves the record existed at a point in chain time.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Verifier shows verified locally, tampered after an edit.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: One of the three roles in the mandate — owner, payer or agent — each with a fixed capability set. Roles never overlap for the MVP.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: The agent is a party, but a party that can only propose.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: The single constitution version currently binding on every determination. Authority must re-read it at dispatch, never cache it.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Constitution v3 is in force when the sixth split invoice is judged.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: State of a constitution version that has been replaced. It stays queryable so past determinations can be explained against the rules they actually used.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: A refusal citing constitution v2 is provable after v4 is published.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: The derived judgement of whether a payee may be paid right now: eligible, new (escalate), quarantined (refuse) or frozen (refuse).
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Eligibility flips to quarantined the moment the digest mismatches.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: The bank digest the owner personally approved for a payee. Distinct from the digest an invoice presents, and the only one Settlement may route to.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Verified digest 41ab…; presented digest 9f2c… → mismatch.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: The owner-signed act of accepting a new bank digest for a payee and lifting quarantine.
ubiquitousLanguage.examples: Owner re-approves the utility's new account after a phone call.

entities.name: Household
entities.description: The single tenancy root: one owner, one payer, one mandate, one constitution lineage. Guards that exactly one in-force constitution version exists.

entities.name: Constitution
entities.description: Append-only lineage of constitution versions. Publishing a new version supersedes the previous one but never mutates history.

entities.name: ConstitutionVersion
entities.description: An immutable snapshot of operator-owned rules: daily cap, per-payment threshold, payee allowlist policy, signature requirements. Addressed by version number and content hash.

entities.name: Payee
entities.description: A biller with a payout address and a verified bank digest, plus an eligibility status (new, eligible, quarantined, frozen). Eligibility transitions are only legal here.

entities.name: BankDigest
entities.description: Deterministic hash over payee routing details (account, routing, scheme). Two equal digests mean identical destination; a mismatch is the scam signal.

entities.name: PayeeStatus
entities.description: Closed set: new, eligible, quarantined, frozen. Encodes whether Authority may allow, must escalate, or must deny.

entities.name: Invoice
entities.description: A bill presented for payment: issuer reference, amount, currency, due date, content hash, presented bank digest, and lifecycle (received, proposed, in-flight, settled, refused, void). Owns the at-most-one-attempt rule.

entities.name: PaymentAttempt
entities.description: The agent's structured proposal for one invoice: attempt id, amount, payee reference and the determination reference. The only artifact the agent can create; carries no authority of its own.

entities.name: InvoiceHash
entities.description: Content hash over the normalized invoice document. Doubles as the duplicate key and the seed of the on-chain nullifier.

entities.name: BilledAmount
entities.description: Positive USDC amount with fixed precision; refuses negative, zero, or over-precision values at construction.

entities.name: AttemptStatus
entities.description: Closed lifecycle: proposed, escalated, approved, dispatched, settled, refused, expired. Transitions are one-way.

entities.name: PaymentIntent
entities.description: The canonical, code-constructed description of one payment: intent id, invoice id, payee, payee address, amount, bank digest, is_new_payee, requires_owner_signature. This exact structure is what the owner signs and what the contract checks. Immutable once issued.

entities.name: Determination
entities.description: The verdict for one intent: allow, deny or escalate, with machine-readable reason codes, the constitution version consulted, the payee status read, and the timestamp of the re-read. Immutable evidence of judgement.

entities.name: CapLedger
entities.description: Per-day ledger of committed and reserved totals across all payees. The single aggregate that makes cross-invoice structuring impossible.

entities.name: Reservation
entities.description: A hold of a specific amount for a specific intent against a specific day. Moves reserved → committed or reserved → released exactly once.

entities.name: Approval
entities.description: An owner signature request and its verified EIP-712 proof, bound to one intent's exact fields, single-use and expiring.

entities.name: OwnerSignature
entities.description: EIP-712 signature bytes plus the recovered signer; valid only if the signer equals the mandate owner and the typed-data digest matches the intent.

entities.name: DeterminationVerdict
entities.description: Closed set: allow, deny, escalate. Deny carries a reason code (digest mismatch, payee frozen, cap exceeded, duplicate, approval invalid).

entities.name: Money
entities.description: USDC amount with chain precision and explicit arithmetic that refuses to lose or invent units during reservation math.

entities.name: SettlementOrder
entities.description: The executable instruction derived from one allowed intent: intent id, invoice id, payee address, amount, nullifier, network, and the code-generated command reference. Owns the at-most-one-transaction rule.

entities.name: ChainReceipt
entities.description: On-chain proof of a settlement attempt: tx hash, block number, confirmations, status (pending, confirmed, reverted), gas, and the anchor tx hash when one was emitted.

entities.name: Nullifier
entities.description: Deterministic identifier derived from the invoice hash (plus mandate scope). Spent-once marker mirrored by the contract's own mapping.

entities.name: PayeeAddress
entities.description: Checksummed EVM address validated at construction; the only destination Settlement will ever encode into a transfer.

entities.name: ChainNetwork
entities.description: Base Sepolia or local Anvil, with chain id, contract address, USDC address and confirmation requirement bound to it so a receipt always knows where it lives.

entities.name: SettlementStatus
entities.description: Closed set: ordered, submitted, pending, confirmed, reverted, abandoned. Drives the single commit-or-release decision in Authority.

entities.name: EvidenceEnvelope
entities.description: Immutable signed wrapper around one domain fact: event type, subject ids (intent, invoice, payee), the fact payload, constitution version consulted, actor, timestamp, and the HMAC over the canonical encoding.

entities.name: Anchor
entities.description: The on-chain write of an envelope hash: tx hash, block, chain id, and the anchored hash. Gives independent integrity and time that no operator can backdate.

entities.name: EnvelopeHash
entities.description: Canonical hash of the envelope including its HMAC; the exact value written to the chain and compared at verification.

entities.name: VerificationResult
entities.description: verified, hmac_mismatch, anchor_mismatch or unanchored, with the failing field named so the console can show precisely what broke.

entities.name: Owner
entities.description: The adult child: the only party with rule-changing and exception-approving authority, identified by an EVM address whose signature is checked against every approval.

entities.name: Payer
entities.description: The parent whose bills are paid. Identity matters for display and consent, but the payer holds no keys and can never authorize anything.

entities.name: Agent
entities.description: The software identity permitted to propose payments. Registered here so Authority can attribute proposals and deny everything else it might attempt; holds no signing material.

entities.name: Cap
entities.description: The daily USDC ceiling applied across all payees in the household, carried on a constitution version. Rejects negative or zero values at construction.

entities.name: Threshold
entities.description: The per-payment amount above which an owner signature is mandatory, carried on a constitution version. Must be less than or equal to the Cap.

entities.name: PartyRef
entities.description: A typed reference to owner, payer or agent capturing the role and its identifier, so events can say who acted without embedding a whole party record.

aggregateRoots: Household, Constitution, Payee, Invoice, PaymentIntent, Determination, CapLedger, SettlementOrder, EvidenceEnvelope

risks.risk: Rigorix OSS integration (rigorix-server + Python SDK execute/approve/audit.read + precondition client outside the agent workspace) is the single biggest unknown and blocks both core contexts.
risks.mitigation: Hour 0–2: spike execute + approve + audit.read against unmodified server; if the precondition hook cannot call our FastAPI service in time, fall back to the Python SDK in-process path and document the narrowing honestly.

risks.risk: EIP-712 approval binding must be verified twice (Python off-chain and PaymentRouter on-chain); a mismatch in typed-data definition silently breaks scenario 5.
risks.mitigation: Define the exact EIP-712 struct once in a shared spec file and generate both the Python encoder and the Solidity struct from it; test a wrong signature early.

risks.risk: Reservation atomicity across HTTP + SQLite: the cap check and the reservation must be one transaction, or split invoices (scenario 4) will pass.
risks.mitigation: Single SQLite transaction with a conditional INSERT/UPDATE on the ledger row; serialize per-day writes; write a 6-way concurrency test.

risks.risk: Wallet/nonce management for dispatch: a timeout retried with a new nonce can double-pay.
risks.mitigation: Order id → single tx hash persisted before send; retries only re-poll the same hash; nullifier reverts treated as refusals.

risks.risk: Base Sepolia faucet, RPC and USDC availability during the hackathon (or a dead venue network).
risks.mitigation: Anvil is the primary demo path; Sepolia receipt pre-recorded and replayed as a labeled live claim. Fund the wallet before the event.

risks.risk: 24-hour timebox vs. six contexts: frontend, contract, authority service, governance wiring, evidence and demo all compete for the same hours.
risks.mitigation: Cut the must/should/stretch line explicitly at hour 8; freeze the API schema by hour 6 so the React app proceeds against mocks in parallel.

risks.risk: Scam detection is only as good as the bank-digest baseline; a payee's first-legitimate digest change looks identical to an attack and will annoy a real user.
risks.mitigation: Frame quarantine as a feature (owner re-approval is one tap), and demo the recovery path, not only the block.

risks.risk: Evidence anchoring per envelope may be too many chain writes for 24 hours.
risks.mitigation: Anchor deterministically for the demo scenarios only; batch the rest and label the batching.

risks.risk: Demo narrative drifts into crypto jargon and loses the impact/UX judging criterion (35 points).
risks.mitigation: Console copy in household language ('Rent paid', 'Suspicious bank change blocked'); crypto appears only as 'settled'.

risks.risk: One-household assumption leaks (hardcoded household id, single owner key) and breaks the README claim.
risks.mitigation: Keep household_id in every key and document the deliberate single-tenant scope.
